content.title: About
content.content: The pork and cheese burrito is a Mexican dish consisting of a large soft wheat tortilla wrapped around a filling of braised pork, melted cheese, rice, beans, and spices. It offers a rich meaty flavor, creamy cheese texture, and a hint of heat from the seasonings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat flour is more common than corn.
Traditional fillings include black beans, but modern versions often use pinto or red beans.
Pork for burritos is frequently marinated in chili, lime, and garlic for a distinctive aroma.
Cheese melts at around 30 °C, creating a stretchy texture inside the burrito.
Burritos are commonly served with salsa, guacamole, and sour cream.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Pork and cheese provide complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice and beans deliver slowly released energy and help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pork contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which support metabolic processes.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Pork and cheese can be high in saturated fats, so individuals with cardiovascular concerns should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Cheese and prepared sauces often contain a lot of salt, which may raise blood pressure.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or casein allergy should choose dairy‑free cheese alternatives.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked pork may harbor pathogens; ensure it reaches an internal temperature of 71 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos are hand‑friendly; cut them in half for easier handling. Warm them in a microwave or on a grill to make the cheese extra melty. Serve with salsa, guacamole, lime wedges, or fresh cilantro.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked burritos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For freezing, wrap tightly in plastic film and place in a zip‑lock bag; they keep well for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before eating.

content.title: About
content.content: Canned crab is crab meat that has been heat‑treated and sealed in an airtight can. It retains a delicate sea flavor, a slightly sweet aroma, and a firm yet tender texture. The product is ready to eat straight from the can and is commonly used in salads, appetizers, and hot dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crab meat is a high‑quality source of complete protein, containing all essential amino acids.
Canning preserves the nutritional value of crab for up to 3–5 years when stored properly.
In most countries the crab is pre‑cooked at temperatures of at least 100 °C for 30–45 minutes before canning.
Canned crab is a staple in Japanese cuisine (sushi, rolls) and in the United States (crab cakes, salads).
Cans often contain a small amount of salt and sometimes vegetable oil to enhance flavor and texture.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Crab provides about 18 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many seafood items, crab is low in fat (≈1 g per 100 g), making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Mineral powerhouse
items.content: Crab is high in zinc, selenium, copper and magnesium, which are important for immunity, antioxidant protection and nerve function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B12, B6 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Small amounts of EPA and DHA contribute to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Crab is a strong allergen; sensitive individuals may experience severe reactions, including anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned crab often contains added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Heavy metals
items.content: In some regions, crabs can accumulate cadmium and mercury; choose products from reputable brands.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Bulging or damaged cans may indicate compromised seals and a risk of botulism.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned crab is ready to eat after opening. It can be tossed into salads, pasta, rice rolls, soups, casseroles, or used as a sandwich filling. For extra flavor, briefly sauté the meat with garlic and herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep the crab in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 3–4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: Peanut‑butter filled crackers sandwich is a crunchy whole‑grain cracker paired with a smooth layer of peanut butter. It is a convenient snack, suitable for school lunches and on‑the‑go eating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first similar snack appeared in the United States in the 1970s as a quick energy source for athletes.
The peanut butter filling usually contains a modest amount of sugar and salt to balance flavor.
Crackers are often fortified with B‑vitamins and iron.
Packaging is typically multi‑layered to keep the product crisp for up to 12 months.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Peanut butter provides about 6 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Peanuts contain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that are beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The snack supplies vitamin E, magnesium, and phosphorus, important for energy metabolism and bone health.

items.title: Convenient energy source
items.content: The combination of whole‑grain carbs and peanut‑fat delivers sustained satiety.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Not suitable for individuals with peanut or legume allergies.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: One pack (≈30 g) contains about 150 kcal; portion control is advised for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Salt and sugar levels
items.content: People monitoring sodium or blood‑sugar should choose reduced‑salt/sugar versions when available.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy straight from the pack, include in a lunchbox, add to salads, or pair with fresh fruit. For a softer filling, briefly warm in a toaster.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the package tightly sealed. For storage longer than six months, keep refrigerated to prevent fat oxidation.
